title.narrative: LINKS: SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT OF COMPETENCY-BASED TRAINING, ASSESSMENT, AND CERTIFICATION PROGRAM FOR ENHANCING TECHNICAL CAPACITY AND EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR HADZABE.

description.narrative: The Hadzabe people of Tanzania have an exceptional knowledge of biodiversity. As both the oldest continual population of East Africa and the last practitioners of a hunter-gatherer mode of subsistence in the region, they have a highly developed knowledge of the natural world, the ecosystem of the Yaeda Valley and Lake Eyasi, the weather and climate system. UNESCO proposes to work with Hadza elders, adults and youth, to identify community members with the most advanced knowledge of wildlife (identification, tracking and trailing of wild animals), and to establish the capacity to train unemployed youth and adults in tracking and trailing, with internationally recognized certification of competence. This project is to be implemented under Intersectoral Programme 3, through the Regular Programme budget. The initiative intersects with the International Decade of Indigenous Languages, the International Decade of Sciences for Sustainable Development, and the elaboration of the Joint Programme of Work on the links between Biological and Cultural Diversity under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
